ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the vertices of $\triangle ABC$ are lattice points of a square grid. What is the value of $\sin B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} By the Pythagorean theorem, we have: $AB=\sqrt{3^2+3^2}=3\sqrt{2}$\\
$\therefore \sin B=\frac{3}{3\sqrt{2}}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$\\
Therefore, $\sin B=\boxed{\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a square grid, and all vertices of triangle ABC are on grid points. Point B is at the lower left, point C is on the same horizontal grid line as B, and C is 3 grid units to the right of B; point A is 4 grid units to the right of B and 4 grid units above B. Reasoning: According to the specified method, taking B as the origin, the vector \overrightarrow{BA}=(4,4), \overrightarrow{BC}=(3,0). The sine of angle B can be calculated using the two-dimensional cross product formula: \sin B=\frac{|\overrightarrow{BA}\times\overrightarrow{BC}|}{|BA||BC|}. The magnitude of the cross product is |4\cdot0-4\cdot3|=12; |BA|=\sqrt{4^2+4^2}=4\sqrt2, |BC|=3. Therefore \sin B=\frac{12}{(4\sqrt2)(3)}=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}.

Then compute \(\sin B\) by the 2D cross-product formula \(\sin B=\frac{|\overrightarrow{BA}\times\overrightarrow{BC}|}{|BA||BC|}\), which gives \(\frac{12}{(4\sqrt2)(3)}=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\).

method.method_draft: Use the grid to recognize the angle geometrically. From the image, side BC is horizontal. Segment BA rises the same number of grid squares as it runs to the right, so BA makes a \(45^\circ\) angle with the horizontal grid line through B.
